candidates.review: Fixes the first candidate's fault: wings folded tight, body about 0.16 m wide at 0.62 m length (target about 0.2 m), clean upright standing posture, scaled legs with three forward toes and a hind toe. Bill as long as the head, deep at the base with a gently curved culmen. Clean topology: one main piece plus three stray triangles, 10 open edges, 1.7% slivers; normalised to 1.9 units long, +y up, bill toward +z. But it lost the raven marks the first candidate had: smooth throat with no hackles, domed crown instead of the flat Roman-nose profile, no nasal bristles, and the tail tip is notched (forked) where a raven's is graduated to a wedge; folded primaries stop near mid-tail rather than near the tip; legs are long and set wide (feet about 0.2 m apart at scale). Reads as a generic corvid, crow-like, until the build script fixes the tail tip and the throat. Build script: close the tail notch and graduate the outer rectrices into a wedge, add a throat-hackle ridge (or accept it, since lod0 at 1,500 triangles keeps little of it), colour the basal third of the upper bill matte for bristles, pull the feet in toward the midline, drop the stray triangles, decimate with X symmetry.

tiers.texture: lod0 only: material 0 (raven_ground), 1024 px base-colour JPEG (134 KB) on its own UV layout. lod1 and lod2 use material 1 (raven_ground_vc), vertex colour only. lod0 also carries the texture as COLOR_0, so it can drop the texture too; a material that uses the map must not also multiply COLOR_0.
tiers.rig: bird template: BODY 0, LEG_A 1 (left), LEG_B 2 (right), TAIL 3, WING_L/R 4/5 (folded arm: coverts, secondaries, tertials; pivot at the shoulder), HEAD 6 (head and neck; pivot at the base of the neck), HAND_L/R 9/10 (folded primaries; pivot at the wrist). Pivots in extras.rig (wing, wrist, head, tail, hip_l, hip_r); extras.rig.folded_wings true: the wings are body geometry, not flight cards, so collapse 0.
tiers.note: Metres, +y up, bill toward +z, origin on the ground between the feet. Scaled to 0.62 m bill tip to tail tip; loose shards and non-manifold fins dropped; legs shortened 15% (toe tops to belly), body lowered onto them; stance squared (the leading right foot moved back 10.5 cm about the intertarsal joint; the right hip still sits 4.5 cm ahead of the left). Texture graded: plumage mean sRGB 33, 40, 50 to 13, 14, 18 outside the gloss band (#0e0f13) and 15, 16, 24 in it (mantle, scapulars, folded coverts toward #3a3f66); legs, toes and bill repainted matte #141416 (mean 19-20) keeping the scale detail; the pale orange iris dark brown #2a1c14, its pale ring plumage-dark. Decimated by Blender collapse with X symmetry. Renders: scratchpad raven_ground/raven_ground_montage.jpg and raven_ground_head.jpg.

candidates.review: The words "for rigging" and "T-pose" gave a heraldic display eagle, not a gliding raven: the bird stands upright in the file (body along +y, belly toward +z, head turned to face the viewer), wings raised at the shoulder and swept down and back, very broad (planform aspect about 2), trailing edge ragged along its whole length so the five fingers do not stand out, tail a round fan, head hawk-like (short hooked bill, domed crown, no hackles or bristles). The wing shell itself is clean and splittable (a closed two-layer shell, 7-12 mm thick in the hand, 15-35 mm in the arm), but the planform is wrong for a raven and re-posing would not fix it.

candidates.review: No directional lighting is baked in: up- and down-facing faces average the same (sRGB luminance 42 and 43), so do left and right (45 and 45); there is per-feather micro-shading and edge highlights, which is what makes it read. Faults: about three times too light and blue (plumage mean sRGB 38,44,53 against #0e0f13), legs and bill grey (luminance about 70, should be matte black), iris pale orange-brown with a light ring (should be dark brown #2a1c14), breast darker than the back. UVs are many small charts (Meshy atlas), so mips bleed at distance. Lit like a Lambert at about 260 px tall it clearly beats flat #0e0f13 vertex colour, which reads as a black hole with no feathers, bill or eye; at ambient distances (under about 60 px) the difference is gone. Worth keeping for the near ground raven after a grade in the build script (multiply to the palette, desaturate the blue, repaint legs, bill and iris by region), downsampled to 1K; ambient tiers stay vertex colour.

candidates.review: A gliding raven: body horizontal, bill forward (+z), back up, long wings straight out with a slight dihedral (tips about 0.1 m above the shoulders at scale), nearly straight leading edge with a wrist bend, five separated outer primaries on one wing and four plus a gap on the other, scalloped secondaries, long heavy bill with a flat crown. Wings are a closed two-layer shell 8-12 mm thick (median) across arm and hand at a 1.25 m span, so no flattening is needed; they meet the body only at the root, so cuts at the shoulder (|x| about 0.10 m at 1.25 m span) and wrist (|x| about 0.37 m, where the leading edge steps back) separate WING and HAND cleanly, and the same landmarks serve a Blender armature. Faults: span to length is 1.56 (raven about 2.0), so at 0.62 m long the span is only 0.97 m; the tail is a rounded fan with slightly shorter outer feathers rather than a wedge; legs hang down and forward with spread toes (a landing reach, not tucked); no throat hackles or nasal bristles; slight left-right asymmetry (one wing a little further forward). Topology: 20,347 triangles, one 20,048-face piece plus a 162-face and smaller shards, 81 open edges, 4.2% slivers; 1.9 units across the span. Renders: scratchpad meshy/corvus_corax/r2/c6_latest_glide2.*

accuracy_notes: Ravens here are told from crows by size, the heavy bill, the shaggy throat, the wedge-shaped tail in flight and soaring. The current player model (wings spread) has no feet detail and a generic bill; the Meshy candidate has the right bill and throat but the wings are too loose. A local birder should check bill depth, throat hackles, tail shape and the standing posture (ravens walk, and hop when hurried).
